item.title: Matsushima Bay Kayaking: Paddle Among the Pine Islands — Guide
item.description: Sea kayaking through Matsushima Bay offers an entirely different perspective on one of Japan’s Three Great Views — paddling at water level between the bay’s roughly 260 pine-covered islets, gliding through narrow channels and sea caves the tour boats can’t reach. Guided tours suit all experience levels, with calm, sheltered waters ideal for first-time kayakers, and sunrise or sunset paddles offering especially striking light on the pines and rock formations.

item.title: Matsushima Bay's Moon-Viewing & Fireworks Festivals — Guide
item.description: Matsushima Bay hosts two of its most atmospheric seasonal events against the backdrop of its 260 pine-covered islands. The autumn Kangetsu-kai (moon-viewing festival) sees the bayfront lit only by candlelight and lanterns as visitors gather to admire the harvest moon reflected on calm water, a tradition rooted in centuries-old aristocratic moon-viewing customs. In summer, a spectacular fireworks display lights up the bay and its islets, with boats and shoreline viewing spots offering dramatic reflections on the water.
